Research life / Personal reflections

How to Find a PhD

By Rohit Shrivastava · 7 min read

Finding a Ph.D is an complex and a long process that requires thinking at professional and personal level. But it is not an impossible task. It is a self development process so enjoy it.

1. Ask yourself why you want to do a Ph.D?

There are plenty of opportunities to be involved in research without joining a doctorate degree such as working as a research assistant/ technician or in industry. So ask yourself what is your goal? Which area of biology interests you? Identify people working in your chosen scientific domain.

If you are looking to make money then you are in wrong profession, try programming in AI, unless you can get a patent on highly sought after formula/technology/method. One can make decent living in life sciences research. Although I do know people who became very successful and rich while working/investing in life sciences research.

2. Start early and look for advertised Ph.D positions and programmes

This is one of the critical step in finding a good Ph.D, start early !!!

Begin with registration on portals such as findaphd.com (list in Ph.D links). Commonly, Ph.D positions are advertised on the University website & dedicated portals.

In case you are interested in working with a specific professor then you can send them an email directly with your CV and cover letter.

3. Identify a topic or lab according to your interests

Read the ads carefully, look at the details of the Ph.D position, skills required, eligibility and requirements for Ph.D. Now try to merge your interests with the details of the proposed research described in the ad.

Don’t choose a topic just because it’s a fancy project, you will be dedicating 3-4 years of your life into Ph.D. So choose a project you like from the bottom of your heart. Also don’t try to waste your time in applying for positions that you desire to get but doesn’t match your skills. Consult and seek advise from your current Professors, mentors and friends regarding research interests. Sometimes others know you much better.

My suggestion is to go for a Ph.D which is interdisciplinary and makes a significant impact on your career in long run. Think from the perspective of how this position and work you will do in next 3-4 years will contribute to your professional development as an independent scientist.

4. Do homework on the selected lab

Once you have decided a topic or lab to work in, the next step is to dig into the research work done in the lab so far. Look at the recent publications from the lab. You may have to read them twice or thrice to understand the work but it will help you assess the quality of the work done in lab and also help you to suggest a potential question for your Ph.D. It will indirectly suggest your future supervisor that are interested in their work and will set you aside from other candidates.

Be careful, not to choose a lab where there are large gaps in the publication frequency or a lab which is publishing in Q3-Q4 journals. Such labs could affect your career. Also consider the members in prospective lab, I suppose it is not good to work in a newly established with nobody to support you.

My suggestion is to work in a lab that is publishing regularly in Q1 journals and has adequate number of people (Post-docs, Ph.Ds, technician) who can train you, support you and help you troubleshoot when things don’t work. It is very difficult for a PI who has left benchwork to help you in these aspects of lab life.

5. How to apply?

In most cases, an updated CV with contact details of 3 referees and an impressive cover letter are sufficient. But sometimes, a statement of purpose or letter of motivation or research summary is also required. Write cover letters and CV well ahead of deadline and get it reviewed by your Professor, mentor or friends. I believe applying for any position is a self learning process as you will see your CV and cover letter will improve after applying to few positions.

– If you are applying to a position in US, Canada, etc IELTS/TOFEL with GRE score are also required.

– If you are applying for a Ph.D programme, it is always recommended to contact the PI you wish to work with. Send them an informal inquiry, discuss with him/her what you wish to do in their lab, how you can contribute to their ongoing research.

– If you wish to work with a specific PI then write an inquiry email to them as early as possible. As, if they don’t have a funded position and they wish to take you, then they may ask you to apply for external Ph.D scholarships (which requires longer than usual preparation time).

Don’t send a general e-mail (looking for a Ph.D position) to 10-20 PIs at once. You will never get a reply and it shows you have no enthusiasm and motivation to go through their work.

My suggestion is to apply for few positions that suits your interests but put in your best efforts. Also modify each cover letter according to the advertised position showcasing that you have the skills that the PI is looking for.

6. Preparing for the first meeting with your PI – Interview

Congratulations !!!

you are successful in gaining the attention of your prospective PI. Most commonly, PI will suggest a date and time for skype interview. Some PIs send you a paper from their lab to discuss during interview. Read it as many times as you can untill you understand the paper completely. But there is no general rule. Overall, it is an informal discussion with your PI about the project you will work on, skills that you can bring in. Also it gives you an opportunity to know your PI, ask specific question like course work, working style, how is the place, social life, etc.

Caution – Don’t try to over sell yourself in the interview, your PI would have interviewed and supervised many students.

My advice is to make clear number of days of leave you will get in an year and the amount of fellowship once your have been selected. Will there be performance based increment? (In Europe, there is no increment or decrease). Will your supervisor help you in finding job/academic position/PhD, etc for your spouse?

In some of PhD programmes, students are asked to visit the university (cost of travelling is refunded) and give presentation of their current or past work followed by an interview. Some programmes are even more tougher beginning with a written exam. Depending upon the number of candidates your PI is interviewing you can get a reply on his/her decision in a week to a months time. Don’t stop applying until you get a positive answer.

7. Preparing for administrative process and final journey

Congratulations !!! you are successful in getting a PhD.

Commonly, at this stage you will be conversing with academic and administrative secretaries, who will guide you through the registration process of Ph.D and regarding visa process. Every university has its own process and so does each country regarding the visa processing.

In most of the universities there is an international office that will provide you with the document that will be required to obtain the visa. Also, it is always good to have an invitation letter from your supervisor accompanying your visa application. However, it is advisable to personally visit country specific website and their documentation requirements for visa and visa processing time. For example, if you are applying for visa to USA from India, it can take from 45-60 days while from other countries it takes max 10-15 days. In case of doubt, you should contact embassy directly.

  • At this stage I want to emphasize that a lot of PIs pay for their student’s airfare and health insurance but don’t assume they have to pay. So better to sort out these things with the PI in advance.
  • Usually universities have on campus housing facilities such as student dorms, but they can be expensive and difficult to get if you are late in reserving a place. Or arrange a short stay at university’s guest accommodation untill you finalise a place to stay. Avoid staying at hotels as it will cost your dearly.
  • In case you have to purchase your air ticket, buy ahead of travel date and always cheaper to buy two way ticket. Also some airlines give discounts to students in airfare or extra luggage allowance. Mind that airlines don’t advertise it, you need to call their call center and ask.
